_doc: Point-in-time fact sheet for CB retrospectives (retro/build_cb.py). In 2008-2009 the company is ACE Limited, listed on the NYSE as ACE (CIK 896159); CB is only the series key and the symbol under which Yahoo serves its history (the BKR and SPGI encoding). Generated from ACE's own filings: every raw figure is read from the row it appears in (kept in 'rows'), every growth rate, margin and rule-T value is computed from those figures. Every value carries a source with its publication date (EDGAR acceptance time, ET; a filing accepted after the 16:00 ET close is dated the next trading day). Decisions: retro/README.md, 'CB'.

history_vintages.why: 'ACE and its direct and indirect subsidiaries (collectively, the ACE Group of Companies, the Company, we, us or our) are a global property and casualty insurance and reinsurance organization' 'The insurance and reinsurance business is historically cyclical, and we expect to experience periods with excess underwriting capacity and unfavorable premium rates.' 'The incidence and severity of catastrophes are inherently unpredictable and our losses from catastrophes could be substantial.' (FY2006 10-K, Items 1 and 1A): the company calls its own business cyclical (the XOM, CAT and GOOG reading), so CYCLICAL; catastrophe losses are the business's own recurring cost, not a substitution theme

eps_first_excluded.2002: a distorted year (the AAPL FY2002 test): the asbestos reserve strengthening the FY2002 10-K lists ('a $354 million net after-tax charge to fourth quarter 2002 earnings') exceeds the year's $100M net income as the FY2006 10-K restates it ($0.27 a diluted share; $0.19 in the FY2002 10-K, before the FY2004 10-K/A restated 2000-2004), and no filing on the restated basis publishes the year without it, so the history and the P/E window start with FY2003 (2001, a loss of $(0.88) a share, precedes it)

quotes: The following is updated guidance for the full year 2007:
Earnings per Common Share are expected to range between $7.15 and $7.50.
Property & Casualty Net Earned Premium Growth is expected to average from 2% to 4%.
Catastrophe Losses included in our estimated earnings are $300 million pre-tax for the second half of the year.
guides.note: P&C net premiums earned growth 2-4% (a component of revenue: no total is derived, the MSFT segment rule); $300M pre-tax of catastrophe losses budgeted for the second half

guides.eps_guide_operating_note: operating income per share, which also removes realized gains and losses (no field: the SPGI eps_guide_amort rule); the 'previous range' of $7.00-7.50 is in no filing
quotes: Operating Income per Share is expected to range between $7.40 and $7.90. The previous range was between $7.00 and $7.50.
Property & Casualty Net Premiums Earned are expected to increase 1% to 3%. The previous range was a decline between 3% and 5%.
Consolidated Net Premiums Earned are expected to increase 8% to 10%.
Catastrophe Losses included in our estimated earnings are $340 million pre-tax ($270 million after-tax) for the remainder of the year.
guides.note: P&C net premiums earned +1% to +3% (previously -3% to -5%, in no filing) and consolidated net premiums earned +8% to +10% with Combined Insurance: components of revenue, no total derived (the MSFT segment rule); $340M pre-tax of catastrophe losses budgeted for the remainder of the year

price_basis: Yahoo's CB series is the stock of the registrant, CIK 896159: ACE Limited (NYSE: ACE) from its 1993-03-25 listing, Chubb Limited after the 2016 renaming. Its one split (3-for-1, 1998-03-03) precedes every date in the P/E window (2003-01-01 on), so every price the models use is the close as traded. The Chubb Corporation, which traded as CB in 2008-2009, is a different company whose history Yahoo does not serve under CB.
